[RAZI-FULL:v29p4/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | Here أعلم is a noun denoting an action, whose weaker verbal government accounts for the preposition ب before its object.

[TABATABAI:53:30-32/r1] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The demonstrative in ‘that is their limit of knowledge’ refers to the worldly life discussed in the preceding verse.
[TABATABAI:53:30-32/r2] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The limit of their knowledge is metaphorically its endpoint: knowledge reaches the world as its object, stops there, and does not go beyond it.
[TABATABAI:53:30-32/r3] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | Because their knowledge stops at worldly life, it becomes their object of desire, concern, and hope; they turn only toward it and find no reassurance beyond it.

[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p50/r5] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | Angels cannot speak or intercede without God's permission; naming them as female and relying on them to evade accountability will not help, for God knows the righteous and wrongdoers.
